Physical installation:
Mount sensor in desired location Verify mounting secure and beam direction correct Network join:
Sensor automatically joins Wirepas mesh network Join time: 1-10 minutes (typical) No manual activation required Verify in Haltian IoT Studio:

Each RADAR has unique device ID (printed on label) Use ID to identify sensor in IoT Studio Reference ID when contacting support for configuration Labeling best practice:
Note sensor ID during installation Map ID to physical location (e.g., “Parking Space A12”, “Loading Dock 3”) Maintain installation records for future reference Advanced Configuration Options Mesh Network Role Sensor can operate as:
End device: Only transmits own data (lowest power consumption) Router: Relays packets for other sensors (higher power consumption) Automatic role assignment:
Wirepas mesh automatically assigns roles Sensors closer to gateway more likely to be routers Optimal network topology managed automatically Manual role configuration:
Typically not needed (auto-assignment optimal) Contact Haltian support if specific topology required Transmission Power Radio transmission power:
Default: Optimized for balance of range and battery life Adjustable: Can increase for challenging RF environments (reduces battery life) Contact Haltian support for transmission power adjustments When to increase transmission power:
Poor signal strength (RSSI < -85 dBm) Long distance to gateway (> 20m, no intermediate routers) RF-challenging environment (metal structures, underground) Trade-off: Higher power = better connectivity but shorter battery life
Configuration Change Process Step-by-Step Configuration Update How to request configuration change:
Identify sensor:
Note sensor ID (from label or IoT Studio) Confirm physical location Determine current configuration (if known) Determine desired configuration:
Sensing distance: Measure and calculate (include margin) Measurement interval: 30s, 60s, or custom Reporting interval: State change + periodic (specify frequency) Contact Haltian support:
Email: support@haltian.com Include: Sensor ID(s) Desired configuration parameters Use case description (parking, loading dock, other) Reason for change (if not obvious) Haltian applies configuration:
Configuration created in Haltian Operations Cloud Pushed to sensor via Wirepas mesh network Update typically applied within 1-24 hours Verify configuration:
Test sensor with vehicle present and absent Confirm occupancy detection as expected Monitor for 24-48 hours to ensure stable operation Report any issues to Haltian support Configuration Rollback If new configuration causes issues:
Contact Haltian support immediately Describe problem (false positives, missed detections, etc.) Haltian can revert to previous configuration remotely Or adjust to alternative settings Multi-Sensor Configuration Management Configuring Multiple Sensors For deployments with many sensors:

Group A: Parking spaces → 2m distance, 30s interval Group B: Loading docks → 5m distance, 60s interval Group C: Custom application → specific settings Provide sensor IDs per group:
List all sensor IDs for Group A List all sensor IDs for Group B Etc. Submit single request to Haltian:

Define standard configurations for your organization Apply same template to new sensors as deployed Simplifies future installations Example templates:
Standard Parking: 2m, 30s, state change + hourly Standard Loading Dock: 5m, 60s, state change + hourly Low-Power Parking: 2m, 5 min, state change + daily Contact Haltian to establish configuration templates for your deployment.
Monitoring Configuration Effectiveness Verification After Configuration Key metrics to check in IoT Studio:
Occupancy accuracy:
Does “occupied” align with actual vehicle presence? Does “unoccupied” align with empty space? Any false positives or missed detections? Signal strength (RSSI):
Maintained after configuration change? If degraded, may need transmission power adjustment Battery consumption:
Monitor battery level trend over weeks Excessive drain may indicate too-frequent measurements/transmissions Last seen timestamp:
Confirm sensor reporting as expected Gap > 24 hours may indicate issue Troubleshooting Configuration Issues False positives (occupied when empty):
Sensing distance too long: Detecting beyond intended zone Solution: Reduce sensing distance Missed detections (unoccupied when vehicle present):
Sensing distance too short: Not reaching vehicle position Solution: Increase sensing distance Obstruction in beam path: Clear obstructions or reposition sensor Rapid battery drain:
Measurement interval too short: Measuring too frequently Solution: Increase measurement interval (e.g., 30s → 60s) Router role: Sensor relaying many packets Solution: May not be avoidable, plan for shorter battery life or add more routers No communication:
Mesh network issue: Sensor not reaching gateway Solution: Add intermediate router sensors, move gateway closer, increase transmission power Default Configurations Reference Parking Space Default Parameter Value Rationale Sensing distance 2 meters Covers most passenger vehicles Measurement interval 30 seconds Rapid detection for high turnover Reporting State change + hourly Real-time state changes, periodic health check Expected battery life ~10 years Optimized for parking use case Loading Dock Default Parameter Value Rationale Sensing distance 5 meters Covers typical dock depth Measurement interval 60 seconds Stable detection, tolerates vibrations Reporting State change + hourly Real-time state changes, periodic health check Expected battery life ~10+ years Extended by 60s interval Configuration Best Practices ✅ Do:
Measure your space before requesting configuration Test configuration with actual vehicles/trailers Document configuration per sensor (map ID to settings) Monitor battery and detection accuracy after configuration changes ❌ Avoid:
Setting sensing distance beyond intended monitoring zone Excessive measurement frequency (battery trade-off) Configuring all sensors identically without considering individual locations Support Resources For configuration assistance:
Email: support@haltian.com Configuration requests: Include sensor ID, desired settings, use case Troubleshooting: Describe issue, provide sensor ID, current behavior vs expected Response time:
Configuration requests: Typically applied within 1-24 hours Support inquiries: Response within 1 business day

Overview Haltian ENTRYWAY produces measurement data that you can access through the Haltian IoT Platform — receive JSON measurements via MQTT Stream API or query via GraphQL Service API.
This page documents the measurement types, payload formats, and how to access the data.
Self-hosted Wirepas gateway? If you operate your own gateways and decode raw mesh messages, see the CBOR Uplink Reference for the binary message specification.
Haltian IoT Measurements The ENTRYWAY sensor produces the following measurement types:
Measurement Type Description entries People who entered since last report exits People who exited since last report batteryPercentage Remaining battery level Entries & Exits The primary measurement data. Reports directional people counts accumulated since the last report interval.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/peopleCounting/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "entries": 3, "exits": 1 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement entries Integer (0+) People who entered since last report exits Integer (0+) People who exited since last report Field name mapping The Haltian IoT API uses entries/exits. These map to the raw CBOR fields in/out in the Wirepas CBOR message.
Reporting behavior:
Reports immediately on first movement detection Reports every measurement interval (default 30s) during continued activity Reports every idle reporting interval (default 1 hour) when no movement — values will be 0 GraphQL query example:
query { measurementLastPeopleCounting( where: {deviceId: {_eq: "6e5f8ac6-a099-44e5-bb28-25fd3d1f47a6"}} ) { deviceId measuredAt entries exits } } Replace these example values 6e5f8ac6-a099-44e5-bb28-25fd3d1f47a6 — your device UUID Related: Configuration — Measurement Interval | Operation — Data Transmission
batteryPercentage Reports remaining battery level. Updated every 6 hours.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/batteryPercentage/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T12:00:00Z", "batteryPercentage": 92 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement batteryPercentage Integer (0–100) Remaining battery percentage Reporting behavior:
Reported every 6 hours Battery life is up to 4 years with 2x AA batteries GraphQL query example:
query { measurementLastBatteryPercentage( where: {deviceId: {_eq: "6e5f8ac6-a099-44e5-bb28-25fd3d1f47a6"}} ) { deviceId measuredAt batteryPercentage } } Replace these example values 6e5f8ac6-a099-44e5-bb28-25fd3d1f47a6 — your device UUID Accessing Data MQTT Stream API Subscribe to real-time measurement events. See Stream API documentation for connection setup.
Service API (GraphQL) Query historical and latest measurements. See Service API documentation for endpoint and authentication details.

Overview Thingsee BEAM produces measurement data that you can access through the Haltian IoT Platform — receive JSON measurements via MQTT Stream API or query via GraphQL Service API.
This page documents the measurement types, payload formats, and how to access the data.
Haltian IoT Measurements The BEAM sensor produces the following measurement types:
Measurement Type Description distance Distance to target surface in mm batteryPercentage Remaining battery level deviceOrientation Accelerometer data (when enabled) distance Reports the measured distance from the sensor to the nearest solid surface.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/distance/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "distance": 350 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement distance Integer (mm) Distance from sensor to target surface. Range: 40–4000 mm Interpretation:
Distance increases → fill level decreasing (material consumed) Distance decreases → fill level increasing (bin filling up) GraphQL Query:
query { measurementLastDistance( where: {deviceId: {_eq: "your-device-uuid"}} ) { deviceId measuredAt distance } } Replace these example values your-device-uuid — your device UUID batteryPercentage Reports remaining battery capacity.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/batteryPercentage/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "batteryPercentage": 87 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp batteryPercentage Integer (%) Remaining capacity. Warning at 20%, critical at 10% deviceOrientation Reports accelerometer data (only when accelerometer is enabled via configuration).
JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "accx": 0.02, "accy": 0.01, "accz": 1.0 } Fields:
Field Type Description accx Float (g) X-axis acceleration accy Float (g) Y-axis acceleration accz Float (g) Z-axis acceleration Use this to detect if the sensor has been tilted or moved from its installed position.
Fill-Level Calculation Convert raw distance to fill-level percentage:
Fill level % = (empty_distance − current_distance) / (empty_distance − full_distance) × 100 Example:
Sensor to full dispenser: 100 mm Sensor to empty dispenser: 800 mm Current reading: 450 mm Fill level: (800 − 450) / (800 − 100) × 100 = 50% Thingsee IoT Message Reference For customers using the legacy Thingsee IoT platform or self-hosted gateways, the raw message format is:
tsmId Event Fields Description 17200 tsmEv=10 dist, status, ambientRate, numberOfSPADs, signalPerSPAD Timed distance report (hourly heartbeat) 17200 tsmEv=9 Same as above Event-based distance report (threshold exceeded) 1110 tsmEv=10 batl Battery level (every 6 hours) 1111 tsmEv=10 accx, accy, accz Acceleration data (when enabled) 1100 tsmEv=11 swVersion, modelCode, psn System startup info For the full mapping between Thingsee and Haltian IoT measurement types, see Measurement Mapping.

Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement ambientTemperature Float Temperature in °C (range: -40 to +85) Reporting behavior:
Reports every reportInterval (default 60s for pod3, 3600s for pod4/rugged) Reports immediately when temperature changes exceed the configured hysteresis threshold (default 0.5°C) Reports on device startup GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: ambientTemperature from: "2026-01-28T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-28T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt ambientTemperature } } Related: Configure weather mode | Operation — Weather measurements
ambientHumidity Reports relative humidity. Available when weather mode is enabled.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/ambientHumidity/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "ambientHumidity": 67.2 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement ambientHumidity Float Relative humidity in % (range: 0–100) Reporting behavior:
Reports every reportInterval Reports immediately when humidity changes exceed the configured hysteresis threshold (default 2%) GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: ambientHumidity from: "2026-01-28T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-28T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt ambientHumidity } } ambientPressure Reports barometric pressure. Available when weather mode is enabled.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/ambientPressure/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "ambientPressure": 1020.9 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement ambientPressure Float Barometric pressure in hPa (range: 300–1200) Reporting behavior:
Reports every reportInterval Reports immediately when pressure changes exceed the configured hysteresis threshold (default 20 Pa) GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: ambientPressure from: "2026-01-28T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-28T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt ambientPressure } } ambientLight Reports ambient light level. Available when weather mode is enabled.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/ambientLight/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "ambientLight": 270 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement ambientLight Integer Light level in lux (range: 0–100,000) Reporting behavior:
Reports every reportInterval Reports immediately when light changes exceed the configured hysteresis threshold (default 100 lux) GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: ambientLight from: "2026-01-28T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-28T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt ambientLight } } magnetoSwitchStatus Reports door/window open or closed state from the built-in hall (magnetic) sensor. Available when hall mode is enabled.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/magnetoSwitchStatus/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "isClosed": true } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of state change isClosed Boolean true = magnet detected (closed), false = no magnet (open) Reporting behavior:
When hall mode = report on change: reports immediately on each state transition When hall mode = report at interval: reports current state every reportInterval Value persists until the next event — if isClosed: true at 10:00, the door is considered closed until the next false event Event-driven data This measurement is event-based, not time-series sampled. To calculate time-in-state, compute the duration between state transitions. See Concepts — Event-Based Measurements for details.
GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: magnetoSwitchStatus from: "2026-01-28T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-28T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt isClosed } } Related: Configure hall mode | Operation — Magneto switch
machineUsageSeconds Reports machine activity duration when the accelerometer is in machine monitoring mode. This is a pre-aggregated value representing seconds of detected vibration activity within the reporting interval.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/machineUsageSeconds/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "machineUsageSeconds": 204 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement machineUsageSeconds Integer Seconds of detected vibration activity in the reporting interval Reporting behavior:
Reports every reportInterval when accelerometer is in machine monitoring mode Value resets to 0 at the start of each reporting interval Maximum value equals the reportInterval duration (e.g., 300 if reportInterval = 300s) GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: machineUsageSeconds from: "2026-01-28T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-28T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt machineUsageSeconds } } Related: Configure machine monitoring mode | Operation — Machine monitoring
batteryPercentage Reports remaining battery capacity. Updated every 6 hours.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/batteryPercentage/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "batteryPercentage": 85 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement batteryPercentage Integer (0–100) Remaining battery level as percentage Reporting behavior:
Reports every 6 hours (21600 seconds) Last reported value is the current battery state (infrequent updates) Plan battery replacement when value drops below 10% GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: batteryPercentage from: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-31T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt batteryPercentage } } How to Access This Data MQTT Stream API (Real-time) Subscribe to receive measurements as they arrive. See the Real-Time Data Streaming guide for setup.
Subscribe to all measurements from a specific device:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/+/{device-uuid} Subscribe to a specific measurement type from all devices:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/ambientTemperature/+ GraphQL Data API (Historical) Query historical measurements via the Data API. Supports filtering by device, measurement type, and time range.
Data API (Parquet Export) For bulk data analysis, export measurements as Parquet files via the Data API. Parquet files contain all measurement types in columnar format optimized for analytics tools like Python/pandas and Power BI.

Overview Thingsee PRESENCE produces measurement data that you can access through the Haltian IoT Platform — receive JSON measurements via MQTT Stream API or query via GraphQL Data API.
This page documents the measurement types, payload formats, and how to access the data.
Self-hosted Wirepas gateway? If you operate your own gateways and decode raw mesh messages, see the CBOR Uplink Reference for the binary message specification.
Haltian IoT Measurements The PRESENCE sensor produces the following measurement types depending on its configured operating mode:
Measurement Type Operating Mode Description movementDetections Mode 2 (default) Count of PIR detections per reporting interval occupancyStatus Mode 1 Binary occupied/vacant state batteryPercentage All modes Remaining battery level movementDetections Produced in Mode 2 (Visitor counter). Reports the number of movements detected since the last report interval.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/movementDetections/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "movementDetections": 7 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement movementDetections Integer (0–34) Number of movements detected since last report. Resets to 0 after each report. Reporting behavior:
Reports every reportInterval (default 60s) when movement is detected Reports every passiveReportInterval (default 3600s) when no movement — value will be 0 Maximum count per minute is 34 (sensor hardware limit) GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: movementDetections from: "2026-01-28T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-28T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt movementDetections } } Related: Configure Mode 2 | Operation — Mode 2 behavior
occupancyStatus Produced in Mode 1 (Occupancy). Reports binary occupied/vacant state — only sent when the state transitions or at the passive report interval.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/occupancyStatus/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "isOccupied": true } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of state change isOccupied Boolean true = area occupied, false = area vacant Reporting behavior:
Reports immediately when state changes (occupied ↔ vacant) Reports current state every passiveReportInterval (default 3600s) as a heartbeat Value persists until the next event — if isOccupied: true at 10:00, the area is considered occupied until the next false event Event-driven data This measurement is event-based, not time-series sampled. To calculate occupancy duration, compute the time between state transitions. See Concepts — Event-Based Measurements for details.
GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: occupancyStatus from: "2026-01-28T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-28T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt isOccupied } } Related: Configure Mode 1 | Operation — Mode 1 behavior
batteryPercentage Produced in all modes. Reports remaining battery capacity. Updated every 6 hours.
MQTT Topic:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/batteryPercentage/{device-uuid} JSON Payload:
{ "measured_at": "2026-01-28T08:52:11Z", "batteryPercentage": 85 } Fields:
Field Type Description measured_at ISO 8601 string Timestamp of measurement batteryPercentage Integer (0–100) Remaining battery level as percentage Reporting behavior:
Reports every 6 hours (21600 seconds) Last reported value is the current battery state (infrequent updates) Plan battery replacement when value drops below 10% GraphQL query example:
query { measurements( filter: { deviceId: "{device-uuid}" type: batteryPercentage from: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" to: "2026-01-31T23:59:59Z" } ) { measuredAt batteryPercentage } } How to Access This Data MQTT Stream API (Real-time) Subscribe to receive measurements as they arrive. See the Real-Time Data Streaming guide for setup.
Subscribe to all measurements from a specific device:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/+/{device-uuid} Subscribe to a specific measurement type from all devices:
haltian-iot/events/{integration-id}/{api-key-id}/measurements/occupancyStatus/+ Data API (GraphQL) Query historical measurement data via the Data API. Supports filtering by device, measurement type, and time range.
Parquet Export Bulk measurement data is available as Parquet files via the Data API. Useful for analytics, dashboards, and data warehousing.

Overview This guide covers how to plan and deploy the complete Haltian Inventory Tracking Solution (HITS) infrastructure across a facility. It explains the spatial rules for placing gateways, EH Locators, and NANO Tags to achieve optimal inventory tracking and positioning accuracy.
For individual device mounting instructions, see:
EH Locator Installation NANO Tag IoT Gateway N8 Installation Prerequisites Before installing infrastructure devices:
Organization active — your Haltian IoT organization is set up and devices are ordered/delivered Haltian Field application is installed (runs on Android devices, iPhone, or iPad) Site setup plan prepared for your premises — which spaces are equipped with HITS (sites, floors, rooms), and planned locations for gateways, locators, and tags Devices on hand: Haltian IoT Gateways with sales box contents Haltian EH Locators with sales box contents Haltian NANO Tags with sales box contents PoE-USB-C adapters for EH Locators (if applicable) Installation tools: Android device, iPhone, or iPad with Haltian Field Ladders or lifter for ceiling-level EH Locator installation Key Terminology Term Definition Router EH Locator operating mode that routes messages to and from the gateway. Can harvest energy from indoor light or be powered via USB-C. Beacon EH Locator operating mode that does not route messages, but increases tag positioning accuracy. Locator Grid The recommended maximum distance between EH Locators that together cover a specific area. Shared Wall A light wall separating spaces that does not fully block the wireless signal. Site Highest level in the hierarchy (e.g., a campus). Building One site can include several buildings. Floor A building can have several floors. Room The largest individual unit of a floor covered with inventory and positioning infrastructure. Zone A specific area inside a room, defined in the application. Does not need dedicated EH Locators in the corners. General Installation Rules Clearances and Grid Spacing Ceiling installations — maintain a minimum of 2.5m (7.5 ft) clearance between walls and the EH Locator Wall installations — maintain a minimum of 2.5m (7.5 ft) distance from the floor and from corners Locator grid — EH Locators can be spaced up to 15m × 15m (50 ft × 50 ft). Larger grids are possible but may reduce positioning accuracy, especially when reflective objects are present. Height — best performance is achieved when EH Locators are placed higher than other elements in the room (e.g., above shelf tops) Gateway Placement Place the Haltian IoT Gateway close to the densest area of routers — where several EH Locators can connect directly to the gateway with line of sight.
Rule of thumb: the gateway should have line of sight to a few router-mode EH Locators.
Improving Positioning Accuracy To achieve more accurate positioning within a grid, add EH Locators in beacon mode to the center of the grid or on the walls. Beacon-mode locators do not route messages but provide additional reference points for tag positioning.
Router and beacon modes are configured using Haltian Field.
Room Layout Examples Large Hall with Short Metal Shelves For data halls or storage rooms with metal shelves:
Place router-mode EH Locators at the grid corners (ceiling or high wall mount) Add beacon-mode EH Locators to improve positioning accuracy within the grid Choose locations where powering is reasonably simple EH Locators should be mounted more than 30cm (1 ft) higher than other objects on the floor Gateway Location The gateway does not need to be at the edge of the room. It can be placed anywhere within the coverage area as long as it has line of sight to several router-mode EH Locators.
Small Room with Short Metal Shelves For small storage rooms (~100 m² / ~1,075 sq ft):
Place router-mode EH Locators at the room corners Add beacons to improve positioning accuracy A single gateway is typically sufficient Medium-Sized Open Premises For open areas (~300 m² / ~3,230 sq ft) such as loading docks:
Use the standard locator grid spacing Add beacon-mode locators to improve positioning accuracy in open areas Shared Walls and Adjoining Rooms Shared Walls Between Zones Thin dry walls can create challenges when different zones are on each side. Follow these principles:
Ceiling-mounted locators — maintain approximately 2.5m (7.5 ft) clearance on both sides of the shared wall Wall-mounted locators — install on only one side of the shared wall, not both sides Adjoining Rooms When connecting two rooms to the same gateway:
Ensure more than one router-mode locator can transmit messages between the rooms In general, it is recommended to use a dedicated gateway in each room for reliable connectivity Things to Avoid ❌ Do NOT:
Install EH Locators on opposite sides of the same shared wall Block devices with surrounding metal surfaces (locators, tags, or gateway) Create excessive distances between EH Locators, tags, or gateway Install near high-power RF transmitters (WiFi routers or similar) Expose to wet conditions (dripping, splashing, or spraying water) Install in excessively dusty environments Exceed the recommended operating temperature of +50°C Install on greasy or dirty surfaces Installation Workflow Once site planning is complete, install devices in this order:
Gateway first — install and verify the Haltian IoT Gateway is online and connected to IoT Center Router-mode EH Locators — install at grid corners, verify mesh network establishment (green Network LED) Beacon-mode EH Locators — install additional positioning reference points, configure beacon mode in Haltian Field NANO Tags — attach to assets and verify they appear in Haltian Field Use Haltian Field to monitor the installation progress — verify each device comes online, check signal strength, and confirm correct operating modes.
Related Documentation EH Locator Overview — Device details and specifications EH Locator Installation — Physical mounting instructions EH Locator Operation — Operating modes, LED states, configuration IoT Gateway N8 — Gateway documentation NANO Tag — Asset tag documentation Location Tracking (RTLS) — Working with position data after deployment

Product Overview Thingsee COUNT is a USB-powered people counting sensor using Time-of-Flight (ToF) laser technology for directional counting in doorways and passageways.
Primary features:
Time-of-Flight (ToF) laser distance measurement Directional people counting (entries and exits) USB 5V powered (continuous power required, no battery) Wirepas Mesh network connectivity Maximum 1000mm passageway width Indoor use, cradle mounting system Detection Technology Time-of-Flight (ToF) Sensor Technology:
Type: ToF laser distance measurement Laser class: Class 1 laser (eye-safe under normal use) Wavelength: Infrared (IR) laser (typically 850-940nm, invisible to human eye) Detection principle: Measures time for laser pulse to reflect off objects (people, floor) Distance accuracy: ±1-5% typical (millimeter precision) Detection range: 0-2100mm vertical (floor to ceiling) Advantages:
Works in darkness (laser provides own illumination) Temperature independent (measures distance, not heat) High precision (millimeter-level accuracy) Simultaneous passage detection (2-3 people side-by-side) Limitations:
Bright sunlight interference (laser wavelength affected) Certain artificial lighting interference (incandescent, fluorescent, halogen) Physical Specifications Dimensions and Weight Sensor unit (with cradle):
Length: Approximately 80mm Width: Approximately 60mm Depth: Approximately 40mm (from ceiling/mounting surface) Weight: Approximately 100g (sensor + cradle + cable clamp) Cradle mounting system:
Cradle: Plastic housing for sensor attachment Cable clamp: Integrated cable management for USB cable strain relief Sensor unit: Detachable from cradle (snap-in design with springs) Installation Requirements Passageway dimensions:
Maximum width: 1000mm (1 meter) Maximum height: 2100mm (2.1 meters, floor to ceiling) Recommended installation height: 230cm from floor Mounting methods:
Tape: 3M adhesive tape on attachment plate accessory (smooth surfaces) Screw: Permanent screw installation with Torx screwdriver (included) Mounting surface:
Ceiling, doorframe top, wall (horizontal orientation) Must support ~100g weight (sensor minimal load) Smooth, clean surface recommended for tape installation Power Specifications USB Power Requirements Input power:
Voltage: 5V DC (standard USB voltage) Current: Typical ~100-300mA (sensor active continuously) Power consumption: Approximately 0.5-1.5W (typical for ToF sensors) Power supply:
Included: USB wall adapter (5V, ≥500mA) Cable: USB A to micro-USB or USB-C (varies by model version) Cable length: Approximately 2-3 meters (adequate for ceiling-to-outlet routing) Power continuity requirements:
Continuous power: Sensor must remain powered at all times No battery backup: Counter resets to zero if power interrupted UPS recommended: For critical applications where count must survive power outages Power Outlet Recommendations Suitable:
Dedicated outlet (not shared with high-power devices) Not controlled by light switch or timer Reliable circuit (minimal outages) Accessible for maintenance (disconnecting/reconnecting if needed) Unsuitable:
Switchable outlets (risk of accidental power-off) Outlets on overloaded circuits (voltage fluctuations) Temporary power strips (instability risk) Network Connectivity Wirepas Mesh Network Technology:
Protocol: Wirepas Mesh (proprietary wireless mesh networking) Frequency: 2.4 GHz ISM band (same as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth) Range: Up to ~20 meters to gateway (direct line of sight) ~10 meters through walls (varies by construction) Extended via mesh routers (other Wirepas sensors act as relays) Network behavior:
Automatic joining: Sensor automatically joins Wirepas mesh after installation Self-healing: Mesh automatically routes around failed nodes Low power: Optimized for battery devices (COUNT is USB-powered, not power-constrained) Data Transmission Measurement data:
Values transmitted: Entries count, exits count, timestamp Data format: JSON payloads via Wirepas mesh to gateway Reporting frequency: Configurable (default typically 30 seconds to 5 minutes) Trigger-based reporting: Optional (report every X entries/exits instead of periodic) Payload example:
{ "measurementDirectionalMovement": [ { "deviceId": "abc123...", "entries": 5, "exits": 3, "measuredAt": "2026-01-20T14:30:00.000+00:00" } ] } Network requirements:
Haltian Wirepas gateway within range (~20m) Or Wirepas routers/repeaters to extend mesh coverage Adequate signal strength (RSSI > -85 dBm recommended) Environmental Specifications Operating Conditions Temperature:
Operating range: 0°C to +40°C (recommended, indoor use) Storage range: -10°C to +60°C (when not powered) Humidity:
Operating humidity: 20% to 80% RH (relative humidity), non-condensing Storage humidity: 10% to 90% RH, non-condensing Atmospheric pressure:
Operating: 86 kPa to 106 kPa (equivalent to sea level to ~1500m elevation) Environmental Protection Indoor use only:
IP rating: Not specified (not designed for outdoor use) No weatherproofing: Not resistant to rain, snow, or extreme moisture Dust sensitivity: ToF sensor lens requires clean environment (dust reduces accuracy) Suitable environments:
Climate-controlled offices, meeting rooms, retail stores Indoor passageways with moderate humidity and temperature Protected from direct sunlight (sun interferes with ToF laser) Unsuitable environments:
Outdoor installations (no weatherproofing) High-moisture areas (risk of condensation on ToF lens) Dusty or industrial environments (lens contamination) Direct sunlight exposure (laser interference) Lighting Conditions Optimal Lighting Works best with:
Moderate indoor lighting (office lighting, overhead LEDs) Consistent lighting (not rapidly changing) Indirect sunlight (ambient light through windows, not direct sun) Lighting Interference Avoid:
Bright sunlight: Direct sunlight on sensor (infrared wavelength interference) Incandescent lamps: Certain wavelengths affect ToF laser accuracy Fluorescent lamps: May interfere with ToF measurements Halogen lamps: High IR output can confuse ToF sensor Rapidly changing light: Flashing lights, strobe effects Mitigation:
Install away from windows with direct sun Use window shades/blinds to reduce sun exposure Choose locations with LED lighting (minimal IR output, compatible with ToF) Performance Specifications Detection Accuracy Counting accuracy:
Single-file traffic: > 95% accuracy (one person at a time) Moderate traffic: > 90% accuracy (1-3 people per minute) Busy traffic: > 85% accuracy (2-3 people side-by-side) Factors affecting accuracy:
Passageway width (narrower = better, up to 1000mm max) Lighting conditions (moderate lighting optimal, avoid bright sun) Installation height (230cm recommended for optimal coverage) Walking speed (normal to fast preferred, very slow may be missed) Simultaneous Passage Capability:
Detects 2-3 people walking side-by-side (within 1000mm width) Higher accuracy than PIR-based sensors for simultaneous passage Very crowded passage (> 3 people simultaneously) may cause undercounting Measurement Specifications Count Data Measurement values:
entries: Integer count of people entering (based on direction configuration) exits: Integer count of people exiting (opposite of entry direction) timestamp: ISO 8601 format with timezone (e.g., 2026-01-20T14:30:00.000+00:00) Counter behavior:
Incremental: Counts increment by 1 for each detected passage Reset on power loss: Counter resets to zero if USB power disconnected No negative counts: Entries and exits always ≥ 0 Reporting Behavior Default:
Periodic reporting (e.g., every 30 seconds to 5 minutes, configurable) Transmits cumulative entries and exits since last report Optional trigger-based:
Report when entry or exit count exceeds threshold (e.g., every 10 entries/exits) Contact Haltian support to configure trigger-based reporting Configuration Specifications Configurable Parameters Locally configurable (via Thingsee Toolbox app):
Entry direction: IN or OUT (determines which direction is “entry” vs. “exit”) Remotely configurable (via Haltian support):
Reporting interval: How often sensor transmits data (e.g., 30s, 1min, 5min) Count threshold: Trigger-based reporting (e.g., report every X entries/exits) Not configurable:
ToF sensor parameters (factory-calibrated) Wirepas network credentials (pre-provisioned) Certifications and Compliance Safety Certifications Laser safety:
Class 1 laser: Eye-safe under normal use (IEC 60825-1 or equivalent) IR wavelength: Invisible to human eye (850-940nm typical) No direct viewing hazard: Safe for use in public spaces (offices, retail, etc.) Regulatory Compliance Expected certifications (varies by market):
CE: European conformity (electromagnetic compatibility, safety) FCC: Federal Communications Commission (USA, RF emissions) RoHS: Restriction of Hazardous Substances (lead-free, environmentally compliant) UKCA: UK Conformity Assessed (post-Brexit UK market) RCM: Regulatory Compliance Mark (Australia/New Zealand) Certification Confirmation For specific certification documents or compliance questions, contact support@haltian.com or refer to the Thingsee COUNT User Guide.
Accessories and Components Included in Package Standard package contents:
Thingsee COUNT sensor unit Cradle mounting system Cable clamp (for USB cable strain relief) USB wall adapter (5V power supply) USB cable (2-3m length) Installation accessories: Attachment plate (for tape installation) Adhesive tape (3M or equivalent, pre-applied to attachment plate) Screws (for permanent screw installation) Torx screwdriver (for screw installation) QR code sticker (on sensor, for Thingsee Toolbox app configuration) Quick start guide (printed card) Optional Accessories Additional components (contact Haltian sales):
Extra USB cables (longer or shorter lengths) Extra attachment plates (for tape installation) UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) for power continuity Wirepas routers/repeaters (to extend mesh network coverage) Comparison to Other Haltian Sensors Thingsee COUNT vs. Haltian ENTRYWAY Specification Thingsee COUNT Haltian ENTRYWAY Detection technology Time-of-Flight (ToF) laser 3× PIR (Passive Infrared) Power USB 5V (continuous) 2× AA batteries (4-year life) Passageway width 1000mm max 1600mm max Installation height 230cm (2100mm detection range) 250cm (2500mm max) Accuracy (single-file) > 95% > 90% Accuracy (simultaneous) > 85% (2-3 people) > 80% (2 people) Lighting dependency Sensitive to bright sun, incandescent/fluorescent/halogen Works in all lighting (thermal detection) Temperature dependency Independent (laser measurement) Requires temp difference (PIR thermal) Power continuity Counter resets if power lost Counter retained (battery-backed) Configuration Local (Toolbox app, QR code) Remote (via Haltian support) Maintenance Minimal (lens cleaning) Battery replacement (~4 years) Use case Higher accuracy, USB power available Battery-powered, wider passageways When to Choose Thingsee COUNT Advantages:
Higher accuracy (ToF laser precision) Better simultaneous passage detection (2-3 people side-by-side) No battery maintenance (continuous USB power) Temperature independent (works in hot/cold environments) Choose COUNT when:
Power outlet available near installation location Higher accuracy required (retail analytics, critical applications) Simultaneous passage common (busy doorways) Ambient temperature varies widely (ToF unaffected by temp) Choose ENTRYWAY instead when:
No power outlet available (battery-powered preferred) Wider passageways (> 1000mm, up to 1600mm) Counter must survive power outages (battery-backed) Bright sunlight or incompatible lighting (PIR unaffected) Warranty and Support Product Warranty Standard warranty:
Duration: Typically 12 months from delivery (varies by sales contract) Coverage: Manufacturing defects, hardware failures (not user damage) Exclusions: Damage from misuse, unauthorized modifications, environmental factors (water, extreme temps outside spec) Warranty claims:
Contact support@haltian.com with device ID and issue description Provide purchase order or invoice number Photos of device and installation may be requested Haltian support determines if warranty claim approved Replacement or repair provided if approved Technical Support Support resources:
Email: support@haltian.com User Guide: Download PDF Response time: 1-2 business days typical Support hours: Business hours (Finland timezone, UTC+2/UTC+3) Support covers:
Installation guidance Configuration assistance (Toolbox app, direction setup) Troubleshooting (detection issues, network connectivity, power problems) Data integration (API access, webhooks, third-party platforms) Custom reporting intervals or thresholds Ordering Information Product Codes Thingsee COUNT (exact product code varies by region and version):
Contact Haltian sales for current product codes and pricing May vary by market (EU, USA, APAC, etc.) due to regulatory certifications Where to Purchase Direct from Haltian:
Sales email: sales@haltian.com Website: haltian.com Authorized distributors:
Contact Haltian for distributor list in your region Quantity Pricing Volume discounts:
Single units available for testing/evaluation Discounts for larger deployments (10+, 50+, 100+ sensors) Contact sales for project-based pricing quotes End of Life and Disposal Product Lifespan Expected operational lifespan:
Sensor electronics: 5-10 years (typical for USB-powered IoT sensors) ToF sensor: Factory-calibrated, no recalibration needed over lifespan Cradle: Durable plastic, 10+ years with proper care Limitations:
USB cable may wear over time (replaceable) Adhesive tape (for tape installation) degrades (~5-10 years, sensor may sag) ToF lens may accumulate dust (clean periodically to maintain accuracy) Disposal and Recycling Environmental compliance:
RoHS compliant (no hazardous substances) Recyclable electronics (follow local e-waste regulations) Disposal:
Do not dispose in general household waste (electronics recycling required) Contact local e-waste recycling facility Remove USB cable and power adapter (recycle separately if needed) Cradle and sensor can be recycled together (plastic + electronics) Battery: N/A (USB-powered, no battery to dispose)
Specifications Summary Quick Reference Table Category Specification Detection Technology Time-of-Flight (ToF) laser distance measurement Laser Class Class 1 (eye-safe) Detection Range 0-2100mm vertical (floor to ceiling) Passageway Width Maximum 1000mm (1 meter) Installation Height 230cm recommended (from floor) Power USB 5V DC, ~0.5-1.5W consumption Power Supply USB wall adapter included (5V, ≥500mA) Counter Reset Resets to zero if power lost (no battery backup) Network Wirepas Mesh 2.4 GHz, ~20m range to gateway Data Transmitted Entries count, exits count, timestamp Reporting Periodic (configurable) or trigger-based (via support) Configuration Thingsee Toolbox app (QR code scan, IN/OUT selection) Accuracy (single-file) > 95% Accuracy (simultaneous) > 85% (2-3 people side-by-side) Operating Temp 0°C to +40°C (indoor use) Operating Humidity 20% to 80% RH, non-condensing Lighting Sensitive to bright sunlight, incandescent/fluorescent/halogen Dimensions ~80mm × 60mm × 40mm (sensor + cradle) Weight ~100g Mounting Tape (3M adhesive) or screw (permanent) Certifications CE, FCC, RoHS, UKCA, RCM (varies by market) Warranty 12 months typical (manufacturing defects) Lifespan 5-10 years (electronics), 10+ years (cradle) Use Case Indoor people counting (offices, retail, meeting rooms)

Drop test: Survives installation handling Vibration: Tolerates loading dock vibrations, vehicle traffic Thermal cycling: Rapid temperature changes Humidity: High humidity environments Shock: Impact resistance Industrial Durability MIL-STD-810H is a rigorous U.S. military testing standard. Passing MIL-STD-810H confirms the sensor can operate in harsh industrial and outdoor environments.
Radar Sensor Specifications 60GHz Pulsed Coherent Radar Specification Value Frequency 60 GHz (millimeter wave) Technology Pulsed coherent radar Sensing range 10 cm to 10 meters (adjustable) Detection angle 17 degrees (conical beam) Resolution ~1 cm distance measurement Accuracy ±5 cm (typical) Detection Capabilities Capability Value Output Binary occupancy status (occupied/unoccupied) Distance measurement Yes (reported in data payload) Object counting No (presence detection only) Motion detection Detects both moving and stationary objects Reflectivity requirements Detects typical vehicles, trailers, large equipment Detection Cone Coverage At different distances:
At 2m (parking): ~60 cm width coverage At 5m (loading dock): ~150 cm width coverage At 10m (maximum): ~300 cm width coverage Calculation: Width ≈ 2 × distance × tan(8.5°)
Battery Specifications Battery Type Specification Value Chemistry Thionyl chloride lithium (LS33600) Voltage 3.6V nominal Capacity 19 Ah Replaceability Non-replaceable Expected lifespan Up to 10 years (typical usage) Battery Life Estimates Based on measurement intervals:
Configuration Measurement Interval Expected Battery Life Parking default 30 seconds ~10 years Loading dock default 60 seconds ~10+ years Low-power custom 5 minutes 15+ years (estimated) Heavy router usage (Varies - relaying packets) 7-10 years Factors affecting battery life:
Measurement frequency (more measurements = faster drain) Transmission frequency (more reports = faster drain) Mesh network role (routers relay packets, consume more power) Environmental temperature (extreme cold reduces capacity) End of Life Battery is non-replaceable. When battery depleted (after ~10 years), sensor has reached end of life and must be replaced with new unit.
Communication Specifications Wireless Technology Specification Value Protocol Wirepas Massive (mesh networking) Frequency 2.4 GHz ISM band Range Up to 20 meters (node-to-node or node-to-gateway) Topology Self-organizing mesh network Encryption AES-128 encryption Network Characteristics Feature Details Mesh routing Automatic multi-hop routing Self-healing Network adapts if nodes fail Scalability Supports thousands of nodes per network Latency Seconds to minutes (typical) Gateway requirement Yes (Thingsee Gateway or compatible) Data Transmission Payload structure (example):

contents:
Overview Haltian ENTRYWAY is configured remotely through the Service API (GraphQL) — named commands with built-in validation and automatic encoding.
This page documents the available commands and provides ready-to-use examples. For detailed parameter explanations and configuration scenarios, see Configuration.
Self-hosted Wirepas gateway? If you operate your own gateways and send raw mesh commands, see the CBOR Downlink Reference for the binary command specification.
Service API Commands The Service API provides named configuration commands that handle CBOR encoding, delivery, and validation automatically. Use these through the Service API (GraphQL).
Available Commands Command Purpose Parameters SetReportAndMeasurementInterval Set reporting and measurement frequency reportInterval, measurementInterval GetReportAndMeasurementInterval Read current intervals — SetPeopleCountingOrientation Set entry/exit counting direction peopleCountingOrientation GetPeopleCountingOrientation Read current direction — SetReportAndMeasurementInterval Configures how frequently the sensor reports data and how often it takes measurements.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Range Default Description reportInterval Integer 60–86400 3600 How often the sensor sends a report to the cloud (seconds) measurementInterval Integer 30–86400 30 How often the sensor checks for movement (seconds) Set 5-minute reporting with 30-second measurement:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "XXCN01TSC20205507" reportInterval: 300 measurementInterval: 30 } ) { success } } Replace these example values XXCN01TSC20205507 — your device vendor serial number 300 — your desired reporting interval in seconds (min 60s, max 86400s) 30 — your desired measurement interval in seconds (min 30s, max 86400s) GetReportAndMeasurementInterval Reads the current reporting and measurement intervals from the device.
query { getReportAndMeasurementInterval( vendorSerial: "XXCN01TSC20205507" ) { reportInterval measurementInterval } } SetPeopleCountingOrientation Sets the entry/exit counting direction. Use this if counts appear inverted after installation — no need to physically rotate the sensor.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Values Default Description peopleCountingOrientation Integer 0, 1 0 0 = normal (factory default), 1 = reversed (swap entry/exit) Reverse counting direction:
mutation { setPeopleCountingOrientation( input: { vendorSerial: "XXCN01TSC20205507" peopleCountingOrientation: 1 } ) { success } } Replace these example values XXCN01TSC20205507 — your device vendor serial number 1 — counting direction (0 = normal, 1 = reversed) GetPeopleCountingOrientation Reads the current counting direction.
query { getPeopleCountingOrientation( vendorSerial: "XXCN01TSC20205507" ) { peopleCountingOrientation } } Quick Configuration Recipes High-Frequency Monitoring 10-minute reporting with 30-second measurement for busy entrances:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "XXCN01TSC20205507" reportInterval: 600 measurementInterval: 30 } ) { success } } Low-Power Long Interval 1-hour reporting for low-traffic areas (maximizes battery life):
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "XXCN01TSC20205507" reportInterval: 3600 measurementInterval: 30 } ) { success } } Fix Inverted Counts If entry and exit counts are swapped after installation:
mutation { setPeopleCountingOrientation( input: { vendorSerial: "XXCN01TSC20205507" peopleCountingOrientation: 1 } ) { success } }

Self-hosted Wirepas gateway? If you operate your own gateways and send raw mesh commands, see the CBOR Downlink Reference for the binary command specification.
Service API Commands The Service API provides named configuration commands that handle CBOR encoding, delivery, and validation automatically. Use these through the Service API (GraphQL).
Available Commands Command Purpose Parameters SetReportAndMeasurementInterval Set reporting and measurement frequency reportInterval, measurementInterval GetReportAndMeasurementInterval Read current intervals — ResetTVOC Reset TVOC sensor baseline — SetReportAndMeasurementInterval Configures how frequently the sensor takes measurements and reports data to the cloud.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Range Default Description reportInterval Integer 600–86400 3600 How often the sensor sends a report to the cloud (seconds) measurementInterval Integer 10–86400 300 How often the sensor takes a measurement (seconds) Set 5-minute reporting with 30-second measurement:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSAR01TSC20204001" reportInterval: 300 measurementInterval: 30 } ) { success } } Replace these example values TSAR01TSC20204001 — your device vendor serial number 300 — your desired reporting interval in seconds (min 600s, max 86400s) 30 — your desired measurement interval in seconds (min 10s, max 86400s) GetReportAndMeasurementInterval Reads the current reporting and measurement intervals from the device.
query { getReportAndMeasurementInterval( vendorSerial: "TSAR01TSC20204001" ) { reportInterval measurementInterval } } ResetTVOC Resets the TVOC sensor baseline. Use when the sensor has been exposed to high VOC levels and needs recalibration.
mutation { resetTVOC( input: { vendorSerial: "TSAR01TSC20204001" } ) { success } } Replace these example values TSAR01TSC20204001 — your device vendor serial number Quick Configuration Recipes High-Frequency Air Quality Monitoring 10-minute reporting with 30-second measurement for meeting rooms:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSAR01TSC20204001" reportInterval: 600 measurementInterval: 30 } ) { success } } Low-Power Long Interval 1-hour reporting with 5-minute measurement for general areas (maximizes battery life):
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSAR01TSC20204001" reportInterval: 3600 measurementInterval: 300 } ) { success } } Reset TVOC After High Exposure If TVOC readings seem elevated after cleaning or construction:
mutation { resetTVOC( input: { vendorSerial: "TSAR01TSC20204001" } ) { success } }

contents:
Overview Thingsee BEAM is configured remotely through the Service API (GraphQL) — named commands with built-in validation and automatic encoding.
Configuration changes can also be requested via support@haltian.com if you do not have direct API access.
Service API Commands The Service API provides named configuration commands that handle CBOR encoding, delivery, and validation automatically. Use these through the Service API (GraphQL).
Available Commands Command Purpose Parameters SetReportAndMeasurementInterval Set reporting and measurement frequency reportInterval, measurementInterval GetReportAndMeasurementInterval Read current intervals — SetDeviceConfiguration Set sensor-specific parameters rangingMode, rangingTimingBudget, rangingROI, accelerometer, temperature GetDeviceConfiguration Read current device configuration — SetReportAndMeasurementInterval Configures how frequently the sensor takes measurements and reports data to the cloud.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Range Default Description reportInterval Integer 600–86400 3600 How often the sensor sends a report (seconds) measurementInterval Integer 10–86400 300 How often the sensor measures distance (seconds) Example — 10-minute reporting with 1-minute measurement:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSTF04TSC20204001" reportInterval: 600 measurementInterval: 60 } ) { success } } GetReportAndMeasurementInterval Reads the current reporting and measurement intervals.
query { getReportAndMeasurementInterval( vendorSerial: "TSTF04TSC20204001" ) { reportInterval measurementInterval } } SetDeviceConfiguration Configures sensor-specific parameters: ranging mode, timing budget, ROI, and optional sensors.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Values Default Description rangingMode Integer 1=short, 2=long 1 Measurement range mode rangingTimingBudget Integer 15,20,33,50,100,200,500 (ms) 50 Accuracy vs power trade-off rangingROIX1 Integer 0–15 4 ROI left boundary rangingROIY1 Integer 0–15 4 ROI top boundary rangingROIX2 Integer 0–15 11 ROI right boundary rangingROIY2 Integer 0–15 11 ROI bottom boundary accelerometer Integer 0=disabled, 1=enabled 0 Optional tilt detection temperature Integer 0=disabled, 1=enabled 0 Optional temperature reporting Example — Switch to long range mode with wider beam:
mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSTF04TSC20204001" rangingMode: 2 rangingROIX1: 2 rangingROIY1: 2 rangingROIX2: 13 rangingROIY2: 13 } ) { success } } GetDeviceConfiguration Reads the current device-specific configuration.
query { getDeviceConfiguration( vendorSerial: "TSTF04TSC20204001" ) { rangingMode rangingTimingBudget rangingROIX1 rangingROIY1 rangingROIX2 rangingROIY2 accelerometer temperature } } Quick Configuration Recipes Dispenser Monitoring (Short Range, Frequent) 10-minute reporting, 1-minute measurement, narrow beam for small dispensers:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSTF04TSC20204001", reportInterval: 600, measurementInterval: 60 } ) { success } } mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSTF04TSC20204001", rangingMode: 1, rangingROIX1: 6, rangingROIY1: 6, rangingROIX2: 9, rangingROIY2: 9 } ) { success } } Large Bin Monitoring (Long Range, Battery Optimized) 1-hour reporting, 15-minute measurement, wide beam for large bins:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSTF04TSC20204001", reportInterval: 3600, measurementInterval: 900 } ) { success } } mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSTF04TSC20204001", rangingMode: 2, rangingROIX1: 2, rangingROIY1: 2, rangingROIX2: 13, rangingROIY2: 13 } ) { success } } Related Documentation Configuration - Parameter explanations and recommendations Data Output - Measurement data formats Service API - GraphQL API reference

contents:
Overview Thingsee ENVIRONMENT is configured remotely through the Service API (GraphQL) — named commands with built-in validation and automatic encoding.
This page documents the available commands and provides ready-to-use examples. For detailed parameter explanations, tuning guidance, and configuration scenarios, see Configuration.
Self-hosted Wirepas gateway? If you operate your own gateways and send raw mesh commands, see the CBOR Downlink Reference for the binary command specification.
Identifying Your Device The exact command names depend on your device model. Check the serial number prefix on your device:
Serial prefix Model Commands used TSEN01 Thingsee ENVIRONMENT SetReportInterval, SetDeviceConfiguration TSEN04 Thingsee ENVIRONMENT SetReportAndMeasurementInterval, individual mode commands Thingsee ENVIRONMENT Rugged Thingsee ENVIRONMENT Rugged (TSEN04R) uses the same commands as TSEN04 devices, plus ActivateDeepSleepMode. See Deep Sleep Mode for details.
Available Commands Command TSEN01 TSEN04 Purpose SetReportInterval ✓ — Set reporting frequency GetReportInterval ✓ — Read current report interval SetReportAndMeasurementInterval — ✓ Set reporting and measurement frequencies GetReportAndMeasurementInterval — ✓ Read current intervals SetDeviceConfiguration ✓ — Configure all sensor modes at once GetDeviceConfiguration ✓ — Read current sensor configuration SetAccelerometerMode — ✓ Configure accelerometer behavior GetAccelerometerMode — ✓ Read current accelerometer mode SetMagnetoSwitchMode — ✓ Configure hall sensor behavior GetMagnetoSwitchMode — ✓ Read current hall sensor mode SetWeatherMode — ✓ Enable/disable weather sensors GetWeatherMode — ✓ Read current weather mode ActivateDeepSleepMode — Rugged only Put device into deep sleep Reporting Intervals Controls how often the sensor takes measurements and sends data to the cloud.
TSEN01 Devices Parameter Type Range Default Description reportInterval Integer 60–86400 60 Reporting interval in seconds mutation { setReportInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN01-xxxxxxxx" reportInterval: 300 } ) { success } } query { getReportInterval( vendorSerial: "TSEN01-xxxxxxxx" ) { reportInterval } } TSEN04 Devices Parameter Type Range Default Description reportInterval Integer 600–86400 3600 Cloud reporting interval in seconds measurementInterval Integer 10–86400 300 Sensor sampling interval in seconds The measurement interval controls how often the sensor takes readings; the report interval controls how often it sends data to the cloud.
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" reportInterval: 3600 measurementInterval: 300 } ) { success } } query { getReportAndMeasurementInterval( vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" ) { reportInterval measurementInterval } } Accelerometer Mode Controls accelerometer behavior — orientation reporting or machine vibration monitoring.
Accelerometer modes:
Value Mode Description -1 Disabled Accelerometer off (TSEN01 only) 0 Disabled / Orientation Off on TSEN04, orientation on TSEN01 1 Orientation / Machine monitoring Orientation on TSEN04, machine monitoring on TSEN01 2 Machine monitoring Reports vibration histogram TSEN01 Devices On TSEN01, the accelerometer mode is set together with other sensor modes via SetDeviceConfiguration. See All Sensor Modes (TSEN01) for the full command.
Value Mode Description -1 Disabled Accelerometer off 0 Orientation Reports 3D orientation 1 Machine monitoring Reports vibration histogram 2 Event-based machine monitoring Reports only when activity is detected TSEN04 Devices Value Mode Description 0 Disabled Accelerometer off 1 Orientation Reports 3D orientation 2 Machine monitoring Reports vibration histogram mutation { setAccelerometerMode( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" accelerometerMode: 2 } ) { success } } query { getAccelerometerMode( vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" ) { accelerometerMode } } Magneto Switch (Hall Sensor) Controls the magnetic/hall sensor used for door and window open/close detection.
TSEN01 Devices On TSEN01, the hall mode is set together with other sensor modes via SetDeviceConfiguration. See All Sensor Modes (TSEN01) for the full command.
Value Mode Description -1 Disabled Hall sensor reporting off 0 Interval Report at every report interval 1 Change only Report only on state changes TSEN04 Devices Value Mode Description 0 Disabled Hall sensor reporting off 1 Enabled Report magnetic/hall information at report interval rate mutation { setMagnetoSwitchMode( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" hallMode: 1 } ) { success } } query { getMagnetoSwitchMode( vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" ) { hallMode } } Weather Mode Enables or disables weather sensors (temperature, humidity, pressure, light).
TSEN01 Devices On TSEN01, the weather mode is set together with other sensor modes via SetDeviceConfiguration. See All Sensor Modes (TSEN01) for the full command.
Value Mode Description -1 Disabled Weather sensors off 0 Enabled Report temperature, humidity, pressure, light TSEN04 Devices Value Mode Description 0 Disabled Weather sensors off 1 Enabled Report temperature, humidity, pressure, light mutation { setWeatherMode( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" weatherMode: 1 } ) { success } } query { getWeatherMode( vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" ) { weatherMode } } All Sensor Modes (TSEN01) On TSEN01 devices, all sensor modes are configured with a single command. You must specify all three parameters together.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Values Default Description accelerometerMode Integer -1, 0, 1, 2 0 Accelerometer behavior hallMode Integer -1, 0, 1 0 Magneto switch reporting mode weatherMode Integer -1, 0 0 Weather sensor enable/disable mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN01-xxxxxxxx" accelerometerMode: 0 hallMode: 1 weatherMode: 0 } ) { success } } query { getDeviceConfiguration( vendorSerial: "TSEN01-xxxxxxxx" ) { accelerometerMode hallMode weatherMode } } Deep Sleep Mode (Rugged only) Puts the device into deep sleep mode. In deep sleep, the device stops all measurements and radio communication to preserve battery. Only available on Thingsee ENVIRONMENT Rugged devices.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Values Default Description deepSleepMode Integer 0, 1 1 0 = disable deep sleep, 1 = enable deep sleep mutation { activateDeepSleepMode( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04R-xxxxxxxx" deepSleepMode: 1 } ) { success } } Quick Configuration Recipes Climate Monitoring Standard environmental monitoring — weather sensors enabled, other sensors off.
TSEN01:
mutation { setReportInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN01-xxxxxxxx" reportInterval: 300 } ) { success } } mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN01-xxxxxxxx" accelerometerMode: -1 hallMode: -1 weatherMode: 0 } ) { success } } TSEN04:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" reportInterval: 3600 measurementInterval: 300 } ) { success } } mutation { setWeatherMode( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" weatherMode: 1 } ) { success } } Door/Window Monitoring Report magneto switch state changes with weather reporting:
TSEN01:
mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN01-xxxxxxxx" accelerometerMode: -1 hallMode: 1 weatherMode: 0 } ) { success } } TSEN04:
mutation { setMagnetoSwitchMode( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" hallMode: 1 } ) { success } } mutation { setWeatherMode( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" weatherMode: 1 } ) { success } } Machine Usage Tracking Monitor equipment vibration patterns:
TSEN01:
mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN01-xxxxxxxx" accelerometerMode: 1 hallMode: -1 weatherMode: -1 } ) { success } } TSEN04:
mutation { setReportAndMeasurementInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" reportInterval: 3600 measurementInterval: 60 } ) { success } } mutation { setAccelerometerMode( input: { vendorSerial: "TSEN04-xxxxxxxx" accelerometerMode: 2 } ) { success } }

contents:
Overview Thingsee PRESENCE is configured remotely through the Service API (GraphQL) — named commands with built-in validation and automatic encoding.
This page documents the available commands and provides ready-to-use examples. For detailed parameter explanations, tuning guidance, and configuration scenarios, see Configuration.
Self-hosted Wirepas gateway? If you operate your own gateways and send raw mesh commands, see the CBOR Downlink Reference for the binary command specification.
Service API Commands The Service API provides named configuration commands that handle CBOR encoding, delivery, and validation automatically. Use these through the Service API (GraphQL).
Available Commands Command Purpose Parameters SetDeviceConfiguration Configure PIR behavior mode, threshold, enableLed, passiveReportInterval GetDeviceConfiguration Read current PIR configuration — SetReportInterval Set active reporting frequency reportInterval GetReportInterval Read current report interval — SetDeviceConfiguration Configures PIR sensor behavior: operating mode, sensitivity, LED indicator, and idle reporting interval.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Range Default Description mode Integer 1–2 2 Operating mode: 1 = Occupancy, 2 = Visitor counter threshold Integer 80–1060 150 PIR detection sensitivity (lower = more sensitive) enableLed Integer 0–1 0 LED indicator on detection (0 = off, 1 = on) passiveReportInterval Integer 300–86400 3600 Idle reporting interval in seconds Set occupancy mode with default sensitivity:
mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" mode: 1 threshold: 150 enableLed: 0 passiveReportInterval: 3600 } ) { success } } Set visitor counter with high sensitivity:
mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" mode: 2 threshold: 100 enableLed: 0 passiveReportInterval: 7200 } ) { success } } GetDeviceConfiguration Reads the current PIR configuration from the device.
query { getDeviceConfiguration( vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" ) { mode threshold enableLed passiveReportInterval } } SetReportInterval Sets how often the sensor reports measurements during active periods.
Parameters:
Parameter Type Range Default Description reportInterval Integer 10–86400 60 Active reporting interval in seconds mutation { setReportInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" reportInterval: 60 } ) { success } } GetReportInterval Reads the current report interval.
query { getReportInterval( vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" ) { reportInterval } } Quick Configuration Recipes Desk Occupancy Monitoring Binary occupied/vacant status with hourly heartbeats:
mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" mode: 1 threshold: 800 enableLed: 0 passiveReportInterval: 3600 } ) { success } } Doorway Visitor Counting Count movements every 60 seconds:
mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" mode: 2 threshold: 150 enableLed: 0 passiveReportInterval: 3600 } ) { success } } mutation { setReportInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" reportInterval: 60 } ) { success } } Installation Testing Enable LED and fast reporting to verify sensor placement:
mutation { setDeviceConfiguration( input: { vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" mode: 2 threshold: 150 enableLed: 1 passiveReportInterval: 3600 } ) { success } } mutation { setReportInterval( input: { vendorSerial: "TSPR04-xxxxxxxx" reportInterval: 10 } ) { success } } Remember After testing, disable LED (enableLed: 0) and increase reportInterval to production values to conserve battery.
For more configuration scenarios and detailed parameter tuning, see Configuration.

Overview Thingsee ENVIRONMENT LONGLIFE is a factory-bundled kit combining the standard Thingsee ENVIRONMENT multipurpose sensor with the Thingsee POWERCOVER extended battery pack, sold as a single SKU for deployments where multi-year, maintenance-free operation is the priority.
This page documents only what differs from the standard ENVIRONMENT. For everything else — installation steps, configuration parameters, message formats, measurement specifications — see the links in Unchanged from Standard ENVIRONMENT below.
What LONGLIFE Changes Parameter Standard ENVIRONMENT ENVIRONMENT LONGLIFE Power source 2× AAA alkaline (own) POWERCOVER: 3× AA Lithium (primary sensor batteries removed) Optional external power — Micro-USB 5V/500mA (via POWERCOVER) Expected battery life Up to 5 years (standard mode) / up to 4 years (machine usage mode) Up to 10 years IP rating IP30 IP30 (unchanged — sensor housing rating is unaffected by POWERCOVER) Weight 35 g with batteries / ~20 g without 107 g (with batteries) Overall dimensions 35 × 35 × 15 mm (sensor only) Sensor 35 × 35 × 15 mm + POWERCOVER 68 × 55 × 30 mm (attached as a single unit) Why the battery swap POWERCOVER replaces the sensor’s own AAA batteries entirely — when POWERCOVER is attached, the sensor’s internal battery compartment is left empty and POWERCOVER becomes the sole power source. This is what extends battery life from ~4–5 years to up to 10 years.
Certifications The LONGLIFE bundle combines two individually certified components:
Thingsee ENVIRONMENT sensor: CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, RCM, MIC, NOM, NYCE, IFT — RoHS, WEEE, REACH compliant Thingsee POWERCOVER: CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA — RoHS compliant For bundle-level certification scope and regional deployment guidance, contact Haltian.
Unchanged from Standard ENVIRONMENT Everything below is identical to the standard sensor — no separate documentation needed:
Installation Guide
POWERCOVER attaches before mounting — see POWERCOVER installation guide for the battery-swap step Configuration Guide Operation Guide Full Technical Specifications — temperature, humidity, pressure, ambient light, accelerometer, magnetic switch specs — all unchanged Troubleshooting Data Output / Uplink Messages Configuration Commands / Downlink Messages CBOR Reference POWERCOVER-specific reporting: the bundle additionally reports battery status and active power source (battery / USB) to the Haltian IoT cloud — see Thingsee POWERCOVER for more information.
Related Documentation Thingsee ENVIRONMENT — base sensor documentation Thingsee POWERCOVER — extended battery pack accessory Thingsee POWERCOVER Installation

Quick Diagnostics Sensor Health Checklist Before detailed troubleshooting, verify these basics:
✅ Power:
USB cable connected to sensor cradle USB power adapter plugged into active outlet Outlet not controlled by light switch (check switch positions) Power adapter LED lit (if equipped with indicator) ✅ Installation:
Sensor securely attached to cradle (springs facing upward, snap sound heard) Cradle firmly mounted (tape adhesion good, or screws tight) ToF sensor lens clean (no dust, dirt, or condensation) Passageway width ≤ 1000mm Sensor centered above passageway ✅ Network:
Gateway operational (check IoT Studio) Sensor “Last seen” in IoT Studio < 10 minutes Signal strength (RSSI) > -85 dBm ✅ Configuration:
Direction configured via Toolbox app (IN or OUT selected) “Configuration successful” message received Entry/exit counts verified with walkthrough test Detection Issues No Counts Recorded Symptom: Sensor shows zero entries and exits despite people walking through.
Possible Cause 1: Power Lost, Counter Reset Diagnosis:
Check “Last seen” timestamp in IoT Studio (if old, power may have been lost recently) Verify USB cable connected to sensor cradle Verify outlet active (test with phone charger or lamp) Solution:
Reconnect power: Ensure USB cable fully inserted into sensor cradle Check outlet: Verify outlet not controlled by light switch (flip all switches nearby) Test outlet: Plug phone charger into outlet, verify it works Restart sensor: Disconnect and reconnect USB power (counter resets, but sensor should come back online) Monitor IoT Studio: Wait 5-10 minutes, check “Last seen” updates Prevention:
Use dedicated outlet (not on switchable circuit) Label outlet “DO NOT TURN OFF - Sensor Power” Consider UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) for critical applications Possible Cause 2: Network Connectivity Issue Diagnosis:
“Last seen” timestamp old (> 10 minutes) No data appearing in IoT Studio despite power connected RSSI weak or missing Solution:
Check gateway status: Verify gateway online in IoT Studio (Devices → Gateways) Check RSSI: If < -95 dBm, signal too weak Move sensor closer to gateway (within ~20m direct, ~10m through walls) Add Wirepas routers/repeaters to extend mesh coverage Restart sensor: Disconnect and reconnect USB power (forces network rejoin) Wait for network join: Allow 5-10 minutes for sensor to rejoin Wirepas mesh Verify in IoT Studio: Check “Last seen” updates Prevention:
Verify RSSI > -85 dBm during installation Document sensor-to-gateway distance in installation records Add mesh routers proactively in large buildings Possible Cause 3: Direction Not Configured Diagnosis:
No entry/exit counts despite people walking through No configuration performed via Toolbox app during installation Solution:
Open Thingsee Toolbox app on smartphone/tablet Scan QR code on sensor Select direction: IN (if sensor inside room) or OUT (if sensor outside room/in corridor) Confirm configuration: Verify “Configuration successful” message Test: Walk through doorway, wait 5 minutes, check IoT Studio for counts Possible Cause 4: ToF Sensor Lens Obscured Diagnosis:
Lens dirty (dust, fingerprints, condensation) Physical obstruction (sticker, label, spider web) Solution:
Inspect lens: Look at sensor “eyeball” (ToF lens on bottom of sensor unit) Clean lens: Wipe gently with dry, lint-free cloth (microfiber cloth ideal) Remove obstructions: Remove any stickers, labels, tape covering lens Test: Walk through doorway, verify counts appear Prevention:
Clean lens quarterly (or monthly in dusty environments) Avoid touching lens during installation Inspect lens during routine maintenance Undercounting (Fewer Counts Than Expected) Symptom: Sensor detects some people but misses many entries/exits.
Possible Cause 1: Passageway Too Wide Diagnosis:
Passageway width > 1000mm Sensor off-center (not equidistant from sides) Solution:
Measure passageway width: Verify ≤ 1000mm If > 1000mm: Install second sensor to cover additional width Or consider Haltian ENTRYWAY sensor (max 1600mm width, battery-powered) Center sensor: Ensure sensor centered above passageway (equal distance from sides) Test: Walk through at different lateral positions (left, center, right), verify all detected Prevention:
Measure passageway width before ordering sensor Choose Haltian ENTRYWAY for passageways 1000-1600mm Document passageway dimensions in installation plan Possible Cause 2: Lighting Interference Diagnosis:
Bright sunlight on sensor (direct sun through window) Incandescent, fluorescent, or halogen lamps near sensor Counts lower during daytime (sunlight) than night (no sun) Solution:
Identify light sources: Look for windows with direct sunlight on sensor Identify incandescent/fluorescent/halogen lamps within 3-5 meters of sensor Mitigate sunlight: Install window shades or blinds (close during bright sun) Relocate sensor to avoid direct sun (if possible) Change lighting: Replace incandescent/fluorescent/halogen lamps with LED lights (ToF-compatible) Test: Walk through doorway at different times of day, verify counts consistent Prevention:
Avoid sensor locations with direct sunlight during site survey Use LED lighting in sensor areas (ToF-compatible) Document lighting conditions in installation records Possible Cause 3: Installation Height Incorrect Diagnosis:
Sensor installed too high (> 250cm from floor) Sensor installed too low (< 200cm from floor) Solution:
Measure installation height: Distance from floor to sensor Optimal height: 230cm from floor (adjustable based on ceiling height) If too high or too low: Relocate sensor to 230cm ± 20cm Test: Walk through doorway, verify counts accurate Prevention:
Measure and mark installation height before mounting (use tape measure) Document installation height in records Possible Cause 4: Very Slow Walking Speed Diagnosis:
People walking very slowly through doorway (e.g., elderly, children) ToF sensor may not detect sufficient distance change Solution:
Test with slow walking: Walk very slowly through doorway, observe counts If undercounting slow walkers: Contact Haltian support for sensitivity adjustment Consider alternative: If slow traffic common, discuss with support (may recommend different sensor or configuration) Overcounting (More Counts Than Expected) Symptom: Sensor counts more entries/exits than actual people passing through.
Possible Cause 1: People Lingering Beneath Sensor Diagnosis:
People stop directly beneath sensor (reading phone, talking) Person shifts position while beneath sensor (ToF interprets as multiple passages) Solution:
Observe traffic: Monitor doorway for people stopping beneath sensor Signage: Post “Keep moving” sign if people frequently stop Relocate sensor: If space allows, move sensor slightly off-center (still within 1000mm coverage, but not directly above common stopping point) Accept tolerance: Some overcounting acceptable if <10% of total traffic Possible Cause 2: Objects Moving Through Diagnosis:
Carts, dollies, or large objects passing through doorway ToF detects distance change (interprets as person) Solution:
Identify objects: Observe traffic for non-person objects (carts, strollers, large packages) Filter in analytics: If downstream system allows, filter out very fast or very slow passages (carts typically faster or slower than people) Accept tolerance: Some overcounting from objects may be acceptable depending on application Possible Cause 3: Lighting Fluctuations Diagnosis:
